H1.note: Signs from the mechanism: risk rises when the TREM2-PLCG2 response is too weak, and INPP5D is the inhibitory arm (title: 'opposed by INPP5D'); the mechanism itself hedges that the protective INPP5D locus does not establish INPP5D's direction. The mechanistic chain ends at plaque compaction and synapse protection (claims 4-9); the disease is reached only by the separate variant associations of H1.4, which no step links to the genes' activity.

H2.note: ABI3 is protective (title: 'protective barrier'); its chain ends at the barrier (claim 2) and reaches AD only through the unconnected GWAS step H2.3. The TREM2 claim is H2.2's: the TREM2-associated state restricts Alzheimer pathology (severity).

H3.note: The chain starts at APOE protein (H3.1), whose overall sign the hypothesis never states; the title's claim is about APOE genotype, and the only signed APOE-to-disease step is ε4 dosage (H3.2), so the APOE claim's subject is the ε4 allele. TREM2 sign from H3.3's note ('a stronger appropriate response is predicted to reduce pathology'); the mechanism hedges (ε4 shifts the program 'toward inadequate debris handling or maladaptive inflammation'), and H3.3's own polarity says the opposite.

H4.no_claim_reason: no direction anywhere: every step has polarity unknown, and the mechanism says 'the causal gene and direction remain less secure'

findings.detail: H3.3 gives the TREM2 lipid response a negative effect on 'restriction of Alzheimer pathology' (so it raises pathology), against its own note ('a stronger appropriate response is predicted to reduce pathology'), the H3 mechanism, and H2.2, which cites the same paper for the same object with the opposite sign.
H1.1/H1.2 end at 'PLCG2-dependent phosphoinositide signaling', H1.3 starts at 'PLCG2-dependent microglial response'; merged as PLCG2 (activity), same node at BioLean's grain, different labels.

H1.3 ends at plaque compaction and synapse protection, H1.4 starts at 'TREM2, PLCG2 and INPP5D variation'; no step says how the risk alleles change TREM2, PLCG2 or INPP5D activity, so the GWAS signals never join the mechanism.

H2.1 ends at the microglial plaque barrier, H2.2 starts at a TREM2-associated state and ends at AD pathology, H2.3 starts at ABI3 variation: three unlinked steps, and nothing in the chain connects ABI3 to TREM2.
H3.2 (APOE ε4 dosage raises risk) stands alone between H3.1 and H3.3; no step says how ε4 changes the TREM2 lipid response, which is the hypothesis's mechanism.
H4.1 ends at 'altered INPP5D/TREM2 signaling threshold', H4.3 starts at 'altered myeloid signaling threshold', and H4.2 (locus association) joins neither.
The H1 mechanism ends at plaque compaction and synapse protection; Alzheimer's disease appears only in the separate, unsigned association step H1.4.
ABI3's only causal step ends at an organized microglial plaque barrier; AD appears only in the unconnected GWAS step H2.3.
All four gene-to-gene or gene-to-signaling steps rest on STRING edges (TREM2-PLCG2 has experimental score 0.00) that cannot carry a direction; the run's notes on H1.2 and H3.1 admit as much.
Reactome over-representation results for the run's own gene set (DAP12 interactions, IP3/IP4 synthesis, CSF1 signaling) are cited as if they stated directed causal steps.

PMID:42092345 reports that mouse Abi3 S212F reduces dense-core plaque compaction and kills microglia via apoptosis and pyroptosis; it says nothing about a microglial barrier, which the run's own note calls an inference.

PMID:28602351 says only that DAM are 'associated with restricting development' of AD and have 'the potential to restrict neurodegeneration'; it tests the Trem2-dependence of the DAM program, not that the state restricts AD, so it is kept only as kind hypothesis (no weight), supporting S9 and refuting S14.
The rs429358 GWAS row has risk allele '?' and trait 'age of onset', and does not name ε4, so it gives no direction for 'APOE ε4 dosage'; the 1993 family study (PMID:8346443) does state the step.
The mechanism and the falsification test speak of correcting 'ABI3 S212F' in isogenic human microglia, but the cited paper says S212F is the mouse numbering (Abi3S212F) of human ABI3 S209F.

PMID:41633359 (supporting) shows INPP5D's SH2 domain represses RIPK1 and that microglial INPP5D deficiency promotes neuroinflammation, TDP-43 pathology and neuronal loss in mice; no step is about RIPK1, and it argues that INPP5D loss is harmful, against H1's INPP5D as the risk-raising inhibitory arm.
R-HSA-2424491 (supporting) is a 'DAP12 signaling' over-representation result (2 of 36 entities) and states no step.
STRING:ABI3-TREM2 (supporting; text-mining 0.63 only, experimental 0.00) is the only thing in the run linking ABI3 to TREM2, and no step uses it.

STRING:PMID:28714976 (supporting) is a publication over-representation result for the gene set (5 of 23 genes); the embedded paper title names rare coding variants in PLCG2, ABI3 and TREM2 without alleles or direction.
rs7412 (supporting) has risk allele '?' (beta 0.435 'decrease' for AD or family history); the run never states a step about rs7412, and with no allele it gives no direction.
rs75932628 (TREM2) is listed as H3 supporting evidence, but no H3 step is about TREM2 variants; it is used only at H1.4.

The H1.3 citation PMID:42357928 calls P522R (rs72824905) 'Alzheimer's disease protective', which states H1.4's PLCG2 part (now under S6, moved_from H1.3), and says it 'is downstream of TREM2', which is closer to H1.1 than the STRING edge but gives order, not sign.

PMID:42357928 names the variant by its protein change (P522R) and the GWAS row by its nucleotide allele (rs72824905-G); matching them rests on both naming the rare missense allele as protective, and the format has no field to record a protein-change-to-allele mapping.

The mechanism says ε4 shifts the TREM2 program 'toward inadequate debris handling or maladaptive inflammation', too little response or a harmful one, so it never commits to whether the TREM2 program protects; only H3.3's note does, and H3.3's polarity contradicts it.

rs28394864 is an intron variant whose mapped genomic context lists ZNF652, PHB1 and others but not ABI3 (ABI3 is only author-reported); the run treats it as 'ABI3 variation' alongside the ABI3 missense variant rs616338.
Three cited GWAS rows (rs429358, rs4938933, rs7412) have risk allele '?', so they cannot give a direction; the run still uses rs429358 for a signed step.

Confidence 'high' and support 'grounded', but the TREM2-to-PLCG2 and INPP5D-to-PLCG2 steps have no directional evidence, the INPP5D direction is hedged in the mechanism itself, and only H1.3 (mouse knock-in) and the GWAS rows hold.
Confidence 'high', but the APOE-to-TREM2 step is a STRING edge, ε4 is never linked to the TREM2 program, and H3.3's sign contradicts its own note.
Every hypothesis lists contradicting_evidence as empty and the run cites nothing as contradicting, though its own supporting citation PMID:41633359 cuts against H1's INPP5D direction.
Every node has an empty curie and empty grounding_evidence, except Alzheimer's disease, which is grounded with the malformed CURIE 'EFO:MONDO_0004975'.
RNPS1 and LPIN2 are left unexplained (the run says so in unexplained_genes); MS4A4A gets a hypothesis with no direction at all.

Four kept GWAS rows are for 'Alzheimer's disease, proxy Alzheimer's disease or related dementias' and one for 'Alzheimer's disease or family history'; kept as AD evidence, but they are composite and proxy endpoints, and BioLean has no way to mark or discount that.

S3/S4 keep PMID:42357928 (title: 'Protection by PLCγ2 Compacts Plaques ... and Protects Synapses'), but the experiment is a protective R522 knock-in vs P522; the direction for PLCG2 activity assumes R522 is a gain of function, which the text never says, and BioLean cannot record that caveat.
BLN:AmyloidPlaqueCompaction: no HP, MP or GO term for plaque compaction (only senile plaques, amyloid beta deposits, amyloid deposition).
BLN:MicroglialPlaqueBarrier: no term for a microglial barrier around amyloid plaques.
BLN:APOE-e4: the APOE ε4 allele is a two-SNP haplotype with no dbSNP ID, and the only corpus term (NCIT:C105364 Apolipoprotein E4) is a protein isoform under a prefix render.py has no kind for.
No HP term for synapse loss; the human-context 'synapse protection' uses the mouse phenotype MP:0015055 decreased synapse density.
Late-onset Alzheimer's disease exists only as a synonym of MONDO:0007089 'Alzheimer disease 2', defined by APOE E4 association, which is wrong for an MS4A4A locus; merged into MONDO:0004975 instead.
No CL term for disease-associated microglia (DAM); 'TREM2-associated microglial state' and 'TREM2-dependent microglial lipid response' are grounded as TREM2 itself.
A dbSNP entity must name an allele, but rs4938933's records name none ('?'); the entity holds an unsigned locus-level association with an allele-less label.
The loss-of-function inversion is written for subjects; here it was applied to objects ('restriction of Alzheimer pathology', 'synapse protection').

The claim-subject rule says use the protein when the chain starts there, but H3's protein (APOE) has no stated sign while the title's directional claim is about an allele (ε4); the ε4 allele was used.

A 'leads_to' step from an allele to disease risk is an effect, but its natural evidence is genetic association (here allele dose in families); association_only would exclude it, so it was kept as observational.

'X-dependent signaling/response/state' labels can be grounded as X's activity or as the process (GO:0048015 phosphatidylinositol-mediated signaling, GO:0001774 microglial cell activation exist); gene-centred was chosen, which joins H1's chain and H2.2 with H3.3.
One mouse knock-in abstract gives S3/S4 belief 0.7 (taxonConsistent false, but not discounted), more than the 0.5 a GWAS row with 128,681 cases gives S5-S7; the taxon gap is flagged, not weighed.
'Alzheimer pathology' was read as severity, so the TREM2 arms reach AD severity and cannot serve the hypotheses' AD-risk claims; no rule relates severity to risk.
